newsitem.title: PERU: Four out of ten in Lima see Fujimori as a dictator.
newsitem.headline: Four out of ten in Lima see Fujimori as a dictator.

text.p: Four out of 10 people in Lima believe they live under a dictatorship, while only three out of 10 think Peru's political system is a democracy, a leading local pollster said on Tuesday.

A CPI poll of 400 people also showed that 85 percent believed Peru was in political crisis because of the government-controlled Congress' dismissal last month of three Constitutional Court judges who had issued rulings opposing Fujimori's bid to run for an unprecedented third term.

Theoretically Peru has a democracy where the judicial, legislative and executive branches put checks on each other's powers. But with a Congress that generally only rubber-stamps Fujimori's law proposals, most Peruvians balked at the threat of limiting the judiciary's checks on the president.
The survey coincided with street rallies last week protesting the Congress' decision to dismiss the judges.

"Due to the government's continuous errors (the opposition) is channelling ... the people's discontent. This is something that has not been seen for years," said Manuel Saavedra CPI's director general, explaining the poll's results to local radio station CPN. He did not say what was the poll's margin of error.

Despite a brief surge in Fujimori's popularity in April when he ordered the rescue of hostages held by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels, the president's approval ratings were currently seen at just below 40 percent -- their lowest since he came to power in 1990.
